items.title: Marshall Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 19, 2021
items.q: I was in that. ... When I got with Sun Ra he just broke — tore that stuff away... I don't have to go out and hire people. ... They come when they want — when somebody comes that means the Creator sent somebody to help us out, to do the part.

ctx.x: Well that attitude served you well trying to fit in with Sun Ra. Can you describe to me what it was that attracted you and compelled you to want to be part of that?

I was working at Revere Camera Company with polishing lenses, filters for cameras you know. I was a polisher, I was polishing. And I used to go to, around the corner to a record store and buy records because I liked to hear all kinds of records. I’m from the old school when all the bands was swinging. So the guy told me, “I’ve got a real nice record for you. It’s a thing with Sun Ra and Cecil Taylor and a whole lot of people is on it.” But I heard this band playing this tune “Super Blonde” and something else, and…
six blocks from where I live, rehearsing every night with the musicians.” I said, “Yeah, okay.” I took my horn when I got out of work that night to meet Sun Ra.
